column4: The working parts of C4 (Collaborative Consent Continuity Controls). Combine to compose a capability; split one to see what it is made of and why.

column5: A folder of atoms, read by path rather than by search.

Partners who keep agreeing as the work moves: the other road to the same place.
Consent kept, and kept again, as things change.
Controls that keep consent continuous: the name says it.
A machine is a house of doors.
Files kept together.

Something said, written down.
A file with its signature beside it: change one byte and it shows.
One fact in one file: the smallest thing C4 keeps.
A folder you need a key for.
Partners working in one shared place.
A game whose rules are recipes: this one.
Hosts that follow the same rules.
Words passed between hosts.

A name that a key can answer for.

A word that opens something because a key agrees.
A name with its own way of speaking.
A note sealed so it cannot quietly change.
Notes that say how, beside the tool that does it.
Two people working as equals.

What a person answers to.
